items.title: Junior Mance Part I interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, New York City, New York, July 27, 1995…
items.q: when I was growing up, because that’s when people like Memphis Slim and Muddy Waters were still living there in Chicago.

ctx.x: That’s a big blues town, isn’t it?

That’s right. It always has been. You know you talk about Chicago blues, nowadays I think it’s a misnomer. I’m not putting down the guys who are doing it now, you know, but the Chicago blues is really, when I was growing up, because that’s when people like Memphis Slim and Muddy Waters were still living there in Chicago. You know, and they had all the joints on the South Side. And I don’t use that word loosely, I mean it, “joints” you know is like what they were playing in. And they had all these great blues…
Not that many of them are still here, that’s too bad.
